newsitem.title: USA: CBOT new crop soybeans end limit down on acreage.
newsitem.headline: CBOT new crop soybeans end limit down on acreage.

text.p: CBOT new crop soybeans ended down the 30-cent-per-bushel daily limit on Monday, hit by news the U.S. Agriculture Department pegged 1997 soybean plantings at 70.85 million acres, traders said.

"The market was caught off guard by the acreage report," said Bob Lekberg, analyst with Goldenberg-Hehmeyer in Chicago. "We ended up with a planting figure that was quite a bit higher than the average guess."
Analysts surveyed by Reuters had predicted plantings at an average of 68.4 million acres. USDA's acreage projection would make this year's planted area the largest since 1982.
Sources said at least six million bushels of soybeans were offered limit down in the November contract. The September, January, March and May contracts also posted limit losses.
Soybeans will trade with expanded 45-cent limits on Tuesday and Wednesday.

Old crop months also ended lower but July was underpinned by a tight quarterly stocks figure and the lack of deliveries posted Monday. USDA put June 1 stocks of soybeans at 499 million bushels, below expectations for 516 million bushels.
Soybeans ended 30 to 16 cents per bushel lower with July down 16 at $7.71 per bushel and November off 30 at $6.17-1/2.

"This was a day full of spreading and it caught the bear spreaders a bit the wrong way," Lekberg said. "The July had been pretty well liquidated in recent session and the rumors of deliveries against the July never materialized."
The July/November spread tacked on 14 cents a bushel to close at $1.53-1/2, premium July.

Several trade sources noted the stocks figure added to suspicions that USDA may have overestimated the 1996-97 soybean crop. USDA has put production at roughly 2.38 billion bushels but some sources contend the crop was smaller.
"The stocks figure suggests that the crop was maybe a tad overestimated but I don't know if we can draw too many conclusions yet," a trader said.

On the day, funds sold at least 14 million bushels, led by Griffin Trading. Griffin reportedly sold 10 million bushels July and six million November but bought four million November, pit sources said.
Commercials were largely on the buy side with Term Commodities accounting for eight million bushels November and four million August.

In options trade, Continental Grain bought 400 August $8.00 calls and sold 400 August $7.80 puts at 26 cents. Continental also sold 250 November $7.00 calls at seven cents and sold 300 November $7.75 calls at three cents.
Volatility was pegged at 28 percent in the August, 22 percent in the September and 20 percent in the November.
Soybean futures volume was estimated by CBOT at 57,000 contracts, compared with Friday's actual volume of 53,098.
